thread:
Mike Chen: FWIW I just noticed traffic skew on routing metrics — looks like two config cohorts became active at the same time and both routed traffic for the same org. quotas doubled for ~2m. 
Ana Patel: Oof. Any immediate mitigation?
Samir Gupta: Can we flip the fail-closed for the new cohort until we fix the evaluation order?
Mike Chen: I already pushed a temporary predicate that forces the newer cohort to 0% via the console (manual override). That stops the overlap but we need a root cause.
Tess O'Neil: Thanks Mike. Do we have a repro? I want a deterministic test to avoid another flip.
Mike Chen: Minimal repro: create two scopes with same priority that overlap (org=1234, region=us-west) and activate both with 10% traffic. When the config propagation race hits both activation workers they both decide to mark matching partitions as active.
Samir Gupta: Sounds like our evaluation is non-atomic across workers. Current pseudocode is: ```for scope in scopes: if matches(req, scope): apply(scope)``` Workers evaluate in parallel and then write TTL-based activation keys. No CAS.
Lee Park: Confirmed. I saw a log where both worker A and B wrote key activation:scope:abcd -> active for partition k, almost same timestamp.
Priya Rao: If the console allows overlapping cohorts at same priority, we should surface a warning and block 100% activations until a uniqueness check runs.
Ana Patel: Agreed. UX change + API validation. For now, can we patch the config service to do compare-and-swap on activation keys? That should make activation idempotent.
Samir Gupta: Yep CAS + add activation-id metadata. When worker reads an activation key it should only write if current value == expected or missing. Also increment a telemetry counter on collisions.
Tess O'Neil: I'm worried about latency impact for high-volume activations. Is CAS going to serialize a lot of operations?
Samir Gupta: It's per-partition and rare. Worst-case we do a low-latency retry loop with jitter.
Mike Chen: Ops: create incident and track customer-facing impacts. @ops-bot can you log an incident and link the dashboard?
ops-bot: Incident INC-5432 created by Mike Chen. Channel: #incidents. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/activations/INC-5432
release-bot: Canary deploy queued: config-service@hotfix/race-cas-2026. Will run 10% of nodes first.
Priya Rao: Can we also add a console validation preventing two active cohorts from sharing exact scope match at same priority? At least block rollouts to 100% until they are disjoint.
Ana Patel: +1. UX: when creating a cohort show an overlap preview and highlight intersections. Use a big orange warning if intersection > 0%.
Lee Park: I'll add server-side validation and a dry-run API that returns intersecting partitions. API sketch: POST /configs/dry-run { scopes: [...] } -> { intersections: [{ scopeA, scopeB, partitions: ["p1","p2"] }] }
Tess O'Neil: Assignments?
Mike Chen: Samir — implement CAS + telemetry (ETA 3d). Lee — dry-run API + validation (ETA 5d). Priya — console warning copy + mockups (ETA 2d). Tess — test plan / deterministic repro and add unit tests for parallel activation paths (ETA 3d). Ana — coordinate rollout with release (ETA today to approve canary).
Samir Gupta: Will add small e2e that spins up 10 workers and asserts only one activation write per partition.
Priya Rao: UX note: show "activation owner" and creation timestamp in cohort details so it's easier to tell which one won a tie.
Mike Chen: Good call. Also add a metric: config.activation.collisions.count with tags for org and scope.
ops-bot: Pager alerts muted for INC-5432 for 30m while hotfix rolls out.
release-bot: Canary started: 2/20 nodes succeeded so far. Monitoring latency + collisions.
Samir Gupta: Hotfix merged to main in PR #4821. Patching release notes: "fix: atomic activation writes to prevent overlapping cohort activation races"
Tess O'Neil: After canary if green we'll roll to 100% and create follow-up RFC for scope deterministic ordering + console intersection UX.
Mike Chen: Thanks everyone. Quick retro: short-term patch + telemetry, medium-term API/UX validation, long-term deterministic scope precedence. I'll update the postmortem in #postmortems after we close INC-5432. :thumbsup:
